question: Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) should always be used instead of enteral nutrition in surgical patients because it avoids the risk of aspiration.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Enteral nutrition is always preferred when the gastrointestinal tract is functional. Benefits: maintains gut mucosal integrity, prevents bacterial translocation, lower infection risk, and lower cost. TPN carries its own serious risks (line sepsis, hepatic dysfunction, refeeding syndrome). TPN is a last resort, not a default.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. The principle is 'if the gut works, use it'. Enteral nutrition preserves gut mucosal integrity, prevents bacterial translocation, is associated with fewer infectious complications, and is far cheaper than TPN. TPN is reserved for patients in whom the gastrointestinal tract cannot be used.
